_about: Proposal paths shown on each parcel. The first path whose 'match' fits the parcel wins, so specific paths come before general ones. match.level = owner type(s), match.county = county(ies), match.owner = a pattern tested against the owner name (case ignored), match.not = a pattern that must NOT match. Templates: add {"name": "...", "file": "templates/..."} to a path's templates list.

match.owner: COLLEGE|UNIVERSITY|DISTRICT BOARD OF TR|DIST BD OF TR|DIST BRD OF TRS|DISTRICT BOARD OF TRUSTEES|DIST BOARD OF TR

paths.title: State college or university land
paths.summary: Owned by a college or university board of trustees, not the school district. Each board has its own real estate and P3 policy.

tracks.name: College P3 policy
tracks.to: The college's facilities or business office
steps: Confirm the owner on the property appraiser record (some of these are private colleges).
Ask the facilities office whether the site is in the campus master plan.
File under the college's P3 policy; Palm Beach State College uses Policy 6Hx-18-4.74.

links.text: Palm Beach State College P3 policy

paths.title: Miami-Dade County land
paths.summary: Two doors. Leasing or buying the land goes through IO 8-4. A proposal that also delivers a public facility adds the P3 track under Code s. 2-8.2.6 and AO 3-65.

tracks.name: Land track
tracks.to: County Mayor, or the commissioner for the parcel's district
tracks.fee: None set by IO 8-4 (you pay public notice costs)
tracks.vote: Majority if the district commissioner sponsors; two-thirds if not
steps: Letter application with a sworn ownership disclosure and proof you are a responsible entity (finances, experience, past performance).

For a direct deal (non-profit s. 125.38, affordable housing s. 125.379, economic development s. 125.045), add the full package: use and public purpose, team, cost and financing, milestones, proposed rent or price.
Mayor refers it to Internal Services within 10 days; departments have 10 days to claim the land; deed and grant checks within 30 days; zoning review within 15 days.
Value: two MAI appraisals over $5 million, otherwise the Property Appraiser's value. District commissioner gets 4 weeks' notice.
Public notice for a direct deal (newspaper, mail within half a mile, or a site sign), at your cost.
You sign the lease or contract first, then it goes to the Board after Commission Auditor review.

tracks.name: P3 track
tracks.rule: County Code s. 2-8.2.6 and AO 3-65, plus s. 255.065
tracks.to: Director of the department the project serves, or Strategic Procurement, 111 NW 1st Street, 13th Floor, Miami, FL 33128
tracks.fee: $25,000 by cash, cashier's check or other noncancelable instrument; extra costs billed, due in 30 days
tracks.vote: Board resolution to authorize a P3
steps: Proposal with everything s. 255.065(4) requires, plus small and community-based business benefits and every obligation you expect from the county.
7 days to cure missing items.
Mayor may decline within 30 days and return the fee.
Evaluation: 90 days under the published code (a 60-day change was proposed).
Mayor recommends a solicitation or rejection; the Board decides. Copies go to the Inspector General and Ethics Commission.

paths.title: Broward County land
paths.summary: No public application route to lease or buy county land. The practical door is an unsolicited P3 proposal under s. 255.065; surplus land is otherwise sold by public bid (s. 125.35).

tracks.name: P3 track
tracks.fee: Set under Admin Code s. 38.40; amount not published online, confirm with Purchasing
tracks.vote: Board finds it sufficient on a preliminary basis, then advertises
steps: Proposal with the s. 255.065(4) contents, a County Business Enterprise participation plan, vendor questionnaire and lobbyist registration.
Confidential pages in a sealed envelope, 3 copies, labeled with the exempting statute.
Cone of silence starts for you on receipt.
Board decides on preliminary sufficiency and advertises for competing proposals (the 2020 Sheridan Street notice ran 51 days).
Board ranks proposals on the s. 255.065 factors.

paths.title: Palm Beach County land
paths.summary: Two doors. Using or buying the land goes through the real property ordinance (s. 22-108). Building or running a public facility goes through Procurement Code s. 2-62 and s. 255.065.

tracks.name: Land track
tracks.fee: $25,000 with the proposal; the county will ask for more if costs run higher
tracks.vote: Supermajority (5 of 7) for any sale, purchase or exchange
steps: Pre-meeting with FDO / Property & Real Estate Management to confirm the parcel is not committed.
Submit to the Department Director with the fee.
Staff may reject without review.
If it proceeds, others may compete; your terms must hold up against a competitor's "not less favorable" offer.
Appraisal; Property Review Committee if the deal assumes a rezoning or departs from appraised value.
Board agenda item.

tracks.name: P3 track
tracks.to: Purchasing / the department the facility serves
tracks.vote: Board: reject, order an evaluation, then accept or reject
steps: File the proposal with the s. 255.065(4) contents.
Board chooses to reject or direct a formal evaluation.
If it proceeds, s. 255.065 notice and a 21 to 120 day competing window apply.
Cone of silence (s. 2-355) once competition is under way.

paths.title: Miami-Dade County Public Schools land
paths.summary: The School Board is its own owner with its own policy. Not IO 8-4.

tracks.name: School Board P3
tracks.to: M-DCPS Facilities / Office of Economic Opportunity
tracks.vote: School Board approval at each stage
steps: Ask whether the site is surplus or part of the facilities work plan.
File under Policy 6327.
Cone of silence applies from receipt.

paths.title: School district land
paths.summary: The school board is a s. 255.065 entity. Surplus land usually goes through the board's own surplus process.

tracks.name: School district
steps: Ask Facilities / Real Estate whether the site is declared surplus.
If not surplus, an unsolicited P3 proposal must serve a school purpose (for example teacher housing or a shared facility).

paths.title: Florida Inland Navigation District land
paths.summary: A special district that holds spoil and waterway management sites along the Intracoastal. Most sites are reserved for dredging.

tracks.name: Special district
tracks.rule: FIND's own rules; s. 255.065 if it can build the project
steps: Ask whether the site is still needed for dredged material.
Leases for public waterfront use are more common than sales.

paths.title: Regional transportation authority land (likely SFRTA / Tri-Rail)
paths.summary: Hospital districts, ports, airports, expressway and other authorities each have their own board and usually their own procurement rules. s. 255.065 applies if the district can build the project.

tracks.name: Special district
tracks.rule: The district's charter and procurement policy; s. 255.065
tracks.to: The district's real estate or procurement office
steps: Find the district's unsolicited proposal or P3 policy on its website.
Ask whether the land is needed for its operations (airports need FAA sign-off on non-aviation use).

paths.title: FDOT land
paths.summary: State land, so there is no s. 255.065 unsolicited path. FDOT sells or leases surplus right-of-way through its district right-of-way office.

tracks.name: FDOT surplus
tracks.to: FDOT District 4 (Broward, Palm Beach) or District 6 (Miami-Dade) Right of Way office
steps: Ask the district Right of Way office whether the parcel is surplus.
Local governments get the first chance at surplus land; partnering with the city or county can help.
Otherwise sold or leased at appraised value, often by bid.

paths.title: State land (TIITF or a state agency)
paths.summary: State agencies are not covered by s. 255.065, so there is no unsolicited P3 path. TIITF land goes through the DEP Division of State Lands.

tracks.name: State surplus or lease
tracks.to: DEP Division of State Lands, or the managing agency
tracks.vote: Board of Trustees (Governor and Cabinet) for most dispositions
steps: Find the managing agency on the property appraiser record or with State Lands.
Ask whether the parcel is surplus.
If a city or county can take title first, partner with it and use its process.

paths.title: Community Redevelopment Agency land
paths.summary: CRAs hold land specifically to get it redeveloped, and they often issue their own requests for proposals.

tracks.name: CRA
tracks.rule: Ch. 163 Part III and the CRA's redevelopment plan
tracks.fee: Set by the CRA (often none for a letter of interest)
steps: Read the CRA's redevelopment plan for what it wants on the site.
Send a letter of interest; the CRA may run an RFP on the site in response (s. 163.380 requires 30 days' public notice before a disposition).
Expect affordability or job commitments in the development agreement.

paths.title: Housing authority land
paths.summary: Public housing authorities are regulated by HUD. They often partner with developers on mixed-income projects through their own solicitations.

tracks.name: Housing authority
tracks.to: Housing authority executive director / development office
tracks.vote: Authority board, plus HUD approval for any disposition of public housing land
steps: Ask whether the site is in the authority's development pipeline.
Disposition of public housing land needs HUD approval (Section 18 or RAD).
Most deals are ground leases with the authority as a partner.

paths.title: Special district or authority land
paths.summary: Hospital districts, ports, airports, expressway and other authorities each have their own board and usually their own procurement rules. s. 255.065 applies if the district can build the project.

tracks.name: Special district
tracks.rule: The district's charter and procurement policy; s. 255.065
tracks.to: The district's real estate or procurement office
steps: Find the district's unsolicited proposal or P3 policy on its website.
Ask whether the land is needed for its operations (airports need FAA sign-off on non-aviation use).

paths.title: City of Pompano Beach land
paths.summary: The city has adopted unsolicited proposal rules under s. 255.065.

tracks.name: City P3
tracks.fee: $25,000 by money order or cashier's check; raised if review costs more; unused part refunded
steps: Pre-meeting with the city.
File with the fee.
Competing-proposal window of 21 to 120 days if the city proceeds.

paths.title: City of Delray Beach land
paths.summary: The city has P3 guidelines for unsolicited proposals.

tracks.name: City P3
tracks.rule: Delray Beach P3 guidelines and s. 255.065
steps: File with the fee.
The Purchasing Manager can decline within 30 days.
Palm Beach County cone of silence (s. 2-355) applies.

paths.title: City of Lake Worth Beach land
paths.summary: The city charges a staff-time fee plus a bid application fee.

tracks.name: City P3
tracks.fee: $5,000 staff-time fee plus $30,000 bid application fee
steps: File with the fees.
Notice runs 21 days and 10 days before the commission meeting.

paths.title: City of Hollywood land
paths.summary: The city sets its unsolicited proposal fee by commission resolution.

tracks.name: City P3
tracks.fee: Set by resolution; ask Procurement for the current one
steps: Get the current fee resolution from Procurement.
File under s. 255.065.

paths.title: City of Palm Beach Gardens land
paths.summary: The city follows s. 255.065 and the county cone of silence.

tracks.name: City P3
tracks.rule: s. 255.065 and the city Procurement Manual
steps: Read the Procurement Manual.
Cone of silence applies.

paths.title: City land
paths.summary: The city's own code governs. Most South Florida cities have adopted s. 255.065 procedures; if this one has not, it must set a fee and process first.

tracks.name: City
steps: Search the city code for "unsolicited proposal" or "public-private partnership".
Ask the City Manager's office whether the parcel is surplus or committed.
Check whether a CRA covers the area; it may be the better partner.

paths.title: Owner needs checking
paths.summary: This owner did not match a known government category. It may be a non-profit, a private lessee or a mislabeled record.

tracks.name: Check the owner
tracks.rule: Depends on who really owns it
steps: Open the property appraiser record and confirm the owner.
If it is a government body, the matching section of the playbook applies.
